steps.reasoning: The candidate threads are available, so the most recent inbound message whose text signals a movie or recommendation request can determine both the recipient and the request context.
steps.action_code:
movie_request_terms = ("movie", "movies", "film", "films", "recommend", "recommendation", "recommendations", "suggest", "suggestion", "suggestions")
request_candidates = []
for thread in laura_candidate_threads:
    contact = thread["contact"]
    for message in thread["messages"]:
        if message["sender"]["phone_number"] != contact["phone_number"]:
            continue
        normalized_message = message["message"].casefold()
        relevance = sum(1 for term in movie_request_terms if term in normalized_message)
        if relevance:
            request_candidates.append({"contact": contact, "message": message, "relevance": relevance})
assert request_candidates
selected_request_candidate = max(request_candidates, key=lambda item: (item["message"]["sent_at"], item["relevance"]))
laura_contact = selected_request_candidate["contact"]
laura_phone_number = laura_contact["phone_number"]
laura_request_message = selected_request_candidate["message"]
laura_request_text = laura_request_message["message"]
print({"recipient": {"first_name": laura_contact["first_name"], "last_name": laura_contact["last_name"], "phone_number": laura_phone_number}, "request": {"message": laura_request_text, "sent_at": laura_request_message["sent_at"]}})

steps.reasoning: The complete note metadata and Laura's request can now be compared using title and tag words, prioritizing explicit title matches and request-specific overlap without relying on fixed IDs.
steps.action_code:
def normalized_words(value):
    cleaned = "".join(ch if ch.isalnum() else " " for ch in value.casefold())
    return set(cleaned.split())
def normalized_text(value):
    cleaned = "".join(ch if ch.isalnum() else " " for ch in value.casefold())
    return " ".join(cleaned.split())
assert all_note_summaries
request_words = normalized_words(laura_request_text)
task_movie_words = {"movie", "movies", "film", "films", "recommend", "recommendation", "recommendations", "suggest", "suggestion", "suggestions"}
request_words |= task_movie_words
stop_words = {"a", "an", "and", "are", "as", "at", "be", "can", "could", "for", "from", "have", "hey", "i", "in", "is", "it", "list", "me", "my", "note", "of", "on", "please", "send", "simple", "some", "that", "the", "them", "to", "via", "want", "with", "would", "you", "your"}
specific_request_words = request_words - stop_words - task_movie_words
normalized_request = normalized_text(laura_request_text)
note_rankings = []
for note in all_note_summaries:
    title_words = normalized_words(note["title"])
    metadata_words = normalized_words(note["title"] + " " + " ".join(note["tags"]))
    normalized_title = normalized_text(note["title"])
    explicit_title_match = int(bool(normalized_title) and len(title_words) >= 2 and normalized_title in normalized_request)
    specific_overlap = len(metadata_words & specific_request_words)
    movie_signal = len(metadata_words & task_movie_words)
    total_overlap = len(metadata_words & request_words)
    score = (explicit_title_match, specific_overlap, int(movie_signal > 0), total_overlap, note["updated_at"])
    note_rankings.append({"note": note, "score": score})
selected_note_ranking = max(note_rankings, key=lambda item: item["score"])
assert any(selected_note_ranking["score"][:4])
selected_note_summary = selected_note_ranking["note"]
print([{"note_id": item["note"]["note_id"], "title": item["note"]["title"], "tags": item["note"]["tags"], "score": item["score"][:4]} for item in sorted(note_rankings, key=lambda item: item["score"], reverse=True)])
verification_targets: Source note selected from metadata using Laura's request
